(p-139) Moreover, if they had devised a way, by building a ramp on their side or by piling up earth, until they could get over it, it would not have benefited them, because they had no means of descending on the other side. This is supported by the fact that they will come out at the end of time by piercing it, not by climbing over it. And the denial of their ability to pierce it does not conflict with what Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi in his *Tafsir*, and Ibn Majah in *al-Fitan* have related from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Ya'juj and Ma'juj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they nearly see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' Then they return to it as strong as ever. Until, when their term is fulfilled and Allah wills to send them out against the people, they dig until they nearly see the rays of the sun, and the one over them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow, if Allah wills,' making an exception. So they return to it, and it is in the same state as when they left it. They dig through it and come out upon the people..." — the hadith. And in the hadith of the two *Sahihs* (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Today there has been opened in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj a gap like this," and he made a circle with his fingers (ﷺ). They both related it from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and in his version: "like this," and he made the gesture of ninety (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 18, verse 98:

So it is as if it were said: What did he say when he poured it out? It is said: ﴿He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord"﴾, i.e., the barrier is a mercy from my Lord, who has been good to me by enabling me to build it and by preventing corruption through it. ﴿But when the promise of my Lord comes﴾, i.e., the nearing of the Hour, ﴿He will make it crumble to dust﴾, by enabling them to breach and demolish it and making that easy for them. The use of the verbal noun in its indefinite (tanwin) form in the reading of the majority, "dakkan," for emphasis in its crumbling, is what the reading of the Kufans points to by the long vowel and without tanwin, "dakka'" (ممنوعًا من الصرف, diptote).

Since this is a matter of great magnitude and a breach of custom, he gave its reason in his words: ﴿And the promise of my Lord is ever true﴾, i.e., the promise He made regarding the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, their breaking through the earth and their corruption in it, and then the coming of the Hour, is certainly to be fulfilled without doubt. Therefore, He helped him in its demolition. On the authority of Qatada, who said: "It was mentioned to us that (p-141) a man - and in another narration: from a man of the people of Madina - said: O Messenger of Allah! I have seen the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj. He said: Describe it to me. He said: Like a striped cloak: a black streak and a red streak. In another narration: a red streak of iron and a black streak of copper. In another narration he said: I reached a land where they have nothing but iron, which they work." Narrated by al-Tabari, Ibn Abi 'Umar, al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin, and Ibn Mardawayh from him, and al-Bazzar by another route, from Abu Bakra (may Allah be pleased with him). Our shaykh Ibn Hajar mentioned this in his takhrij of the hadiths of al-Kashshaf. And in the hadith of the opening of the gate from the biography of the hafiz Abu al-Rabi' ibn Salim al-Kala'i and his shaykh Ibn Hubaysh, (who was the commander of those armies in which was 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rabi'a in the days of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him), its text is: Matar ibn Thalj al-Tamimi narrated, saying: I entered upon 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Rabi'a at the gate, and Shahrbaraz was with him - meaning: he was the king of the gate on behalf of the family of Kisra. A man with a pale complexion came and sat with Shahrbaraz, and they conversed. Then Shahrbaraz said to 'Abd al-Rahman: O Amir! Do you know where this man has come from? I sent him years ago toward the barrier to look into its condition and what lies beyond it, (p-142) and I provided him with great wealth, wrote for him to those near me, gave him gifts, and asked him to write to those beyond him, and I provided a gift for every king. He did this with every king between me and him, until he reached the king in whose land the barrier lies. He wrote for him to his governor over that region, so he came to him, and he sent with him his falconer and his eagle. He mentioned that he treated the falconer well, and said: The falconer thanked me. When we arrived, there were two mountains between which was a barrier closed, rising above the two mountains after they had been level with it, and below the barrier was a trench blacker than night because of its depth. I looked at that and examined it closely. Then I went to leave, and the falconer said to me: Wait a moment! I will reward you: no king succeeds another king except that he draws near to Allah Most High with the best of what he has of the world, and throws it into this flame. He cut a piece of flesh he had with him and threw it into that air, and the eagle swooped down upon it. He said: If it catches it before it falls, there is nothing; and if it does not catch it until it falls, that is something. It came out at us with the flesh in its talons, and in it was a ruby, which he gave to me. It is this one. Shahrbaraz took it from him, and it was red, and handed it to 'Abd al-Rahman, who looked at it, then returned it to him. Shahrbaraz said: This is better than this city - meaning the gate - and by Allah! You are dearer to me in rule than the family of Kisra. If I were in their authority and news of it reached them, they would seize it from me. By Allah! Nothing will stand for you as long as you keep faith, or as long as your greatest king keeps faith. Then 'Abd al-Rahman turned to the messenger and said: What is the state of the rampart and what is it like? He said: It is this garment on this man, and he pointed to Matar ibn Thalj, who was wearing a Yemeni cloak of striped weave whose ground was red and whose pattern was black, or whose pattern was red and whose ground was black. Matar said: By Allah, the man has spoken the truth! He has reached and seen. 'Abd al-Rahman said: Indeed! And he described the nature of the iron and the brass, and recited: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾ [al-Kahf: 96] to the end of the verse. 'Abd al-Rahman said to Shahrbaraz: How much was your gift? He said: The value of a hundred thousand in this land of mine, and three thousand thousand or more in those lands. End of quote. It has become clear that what they challenged about, the two stories of the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn and what is inserted between them, as a rebuke to the Jews who commanded them to ask this, and the story of Musa (peace be upon him) which points to the establishment of the Hour, all of it becomes the greatest binding proof against them if they accept it, and the clearest exposure of their obstinacy if they reject it.

ولَمّا انْقَضى ما سَألُوا عَنْهُ عَلى أحْسَنِ وجْهٍ في أبْلَغِ سِياقٍ وأبْدَعِ تَناسُبٍ، وأدْرَجَ في خِلالِهِ ما أدْرَجَ مِنَ التَّذْكِيرِ والوَعْظِ، والأمْرِ والنَّهْيِ، (p-١٤٤) والوَعْدِ والوَعِيدِ، والتَّرْغِيبِ والتَّرْهِيبِ، والتَّبْكِيتِ لِلْكاتِمِينَ لِما عِنْدَهم مِنَ العِلْمِ، النّاكِبِينَ عَمّا اسْتَبانَ لَهم مِنَ الطَّرِيقِ اللّاحِبِ والمَنهَجِ الواضِحِ صُنْعَ القادِرِ الحَكِيمِ الَّذِي لا يَسْتَخِفُّهُ ضَجَرٌ فَيَسْتَعْجِلُ، ولا يَعِيبُهُ أمْرٌ فَيَسْتَمْهِلُ، وخَتَمَهُ بِما هو عِلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ لِلسّاعَةِ، ذَكَرَ ما يَكُونُ إذْ ذاكَ وما يَكُونُ بَعْدَهُ إلى حُصُولِ كُلٍّ مِنَ الفَرِيقَيْنِ في دارِهِ ومَحَلِّ اسْتِقْرارِهِ؛ ولَمّا كانَ ذَلِكَ أمْرًا عَظِيمًا، دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ بِالنُّونِ فَقالَ عاطِفًا عَلى ما تَقْدِيرُهُ: فَقَدْ بانَ أمْرُ ذِي القَرْنَيْنِ أيَّ بَيانٍ، وصَدَقَ في قَوْلِهِ ﴿When the promise of my Lord comes﴾ [الكهف: ٩٨] فَإنَّهُ إذا جاءَ وعْدُنا جَعَلْناهُ بِقُدْرَتِنا الَّتِي نُؤْتِيها لِيَأْجُوجَ ومَأْجُوجَ دَكّاءَ فَأخْرَجْناهم عَلى النّاسِ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِ الدَّجّالِ (al-Dajjal, the Antichrist): ﴿And We will leave some of them﴾ أيْ بَعْضَ مَن خَلْفَ السَّدِّ ومَن أمامَهُ ﴿on that day﴾ أيْ إذْ جَعَلْنا السَّدَّ دَكّاءَ وخَرَجُوا مُقَدِّمَتُهم بِالشّامِ وساقِطَتُهم بِخُراسانَ، وهم - كَما قالَ اللَّهُ تَعالى - ﴿from every elevation they will swarm﴾ “يَمُوجُ” (yamuju, meaning: it surges and agitates) أيْ يَضْطَرِبُ ﴿among one another﴾ كَما يَمُوجُ البَحْرُ، فَأهْلَكُوا ما مَرُّوا عَلَيْهِ مِن شَيْءٍ إلّا ما أرادَ اللَّهُ، ثُمَّ أبادَهُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَهم وبِقُرْبِ ذَلِكَ أفْنى الخَلائِقَ أجْمَعِينَ ﴿and the Trumpet is blown﴾ أيِ النَّفْخَةُ الثّانِيَةُ لِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿so We will gather them﴾ ويَجُوزُ أنْ تَكُونَ هَذِهِ الفاءُ الفَصِيحَةَ (al-fa' al-fasiha, the "eloquent fa'" that indicates an implied condition) فَيَكُونَ المُرادُ النَّفْخَةَ الأُولى، أوْ ونُفِخَ [فِي الصُّورِ -] فَماتَ الخَلائِقُ (p-١٤٥) كُلُّهُمْ، فَبَلِيَتْ أجْسامُهُمْ، وتَفَتَّتَتْ عِظامُهُمْ، كَما كانَ مَن تَقَدَّمَهُمْ، ثُمَّ نُفِخَ [فِيهِ -] النَّفْخَةُ الثّانِيَةُ فَجَمَعْناهم مِنَ التُّرابِ بَعْدَ تَمَزُّقِهِمْ فِيهِ، وتَفَرُّقِهِمْ في أقْطارِ الأرْضِ بِالسُّيُولِ والرِّياحِ وغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ ﴿as one gathering﴾ فَأقَمْناهم دَفْعَةً واحِدَةً كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ، وحَشَرْناهم إلى المَوْقِفِ لِلْحِسابِ ثُمَّ العِقابِ أوِ الثَّوابِ.

﴿And We will present﴾, i.e., We will make manifest, ﴿Hell on that Day﴾, i.e., when We have gathered them for that purpose, ﴿to the disbelievers, presented plainly﴾, i.e., clearly displayed to them, with all the terrors that are in it, while they find no way of escape from it;

Then He described them with what necessitated their imprisonment in it and its frowning upon them, so He said: ﴿Those whose eyes were﴾ in a state so established that it was as if it were their innate nature, ﴿in a covering from My remembrance﴾, the eyes being the visible and the inward (heart) ones, ﴿by not reflecting upon what We placed upon the earth of adornment as a sign of the Hour, by its annihilation after its revival and its return after its origination﴾; ﴿and they were﴾ by what We had created them upon, ﴿unable﴾, meaning with a great ability that would make them happy, because of the weakness of their minds and the drowning of their insight in their trivialities, ﴿to hear﴾ My verses, which make the deaf hear and the blind see. This is more forceful in rebuking them for their dullness and reproaching them for their stupidity than the mere negation of sight and hearing, because that does not negate capability.

Then he turned to what that had implied, addressing them with rebuke and reproach: ﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me?﴾ That is, did they cover their eyes against My signs and deafen their ears to My words, and worship My servants, supposing them (to be gods) because of the weakness of their intellects? He said ﴿those who disbelieved﴾ to indicate the attribute that necessitated this for them. ﴿That they may take﴾ — that is, even if they exerted every effort — ﴿My servants﴾ from among the living, such as the angels, 'Uzayr and al-Masih, and from among the dead, such as the idols.

Since everything is other than Him, glory be to Him, and since no single thing encompasses all that is beneath its rank among the ranks, he affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿besides Me as protectors﴾ — that is, initiating their taking (them) without My permission. The second object of "hasiba" (to think) is omitted, its estimate being: they help them, ward off (harm) from them, make some of them offspring, and I will not punish them. Since the ultimate purpose of taking a protector is that he does what a near relative does of support and protection from every harm, it is permissible for this to stand in place of the two objects of "hasiba," because its meaning is: did they suppose that taking them would prevent them from Me? Since the meaning of the interrogation of denunciation is: the matter is not so, but rather their flint has failed, their fortune has been lost, and their good luck has vanished, his statement, emphasizing it to refute their claim, is very fitting: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell﴾ — which was previously mentioned, that We presented it to them — ﴿as a hospitable abode for the disbelievers﴾, which we bring forward for them at the first of their arrival, as a guest is hastened to be received, so none can prevent it from them; and for them beyond it is that which is considered insignificant in comparison to it, as is the case with what follows the nuzul (hospitable provision) in comparison to it.

[p. 147]

When it had become clear, through that about which there is no doubt, that they had incurred a loss with no gain in it, and that what they had hoped for had failed, He commanded him to alert them to this, so He said: ﴿Say, "Shall We inform you"﴾, that is, "We inform you, I and every servant of God whose eye is not veiled from the remembrance and whose hearing is not incapable of comprehension, with a great informing, O you who abandon the one who has no creator and no provider besides Him, and who turn toward the one who has nothing in his hand of creation, provision, or anything else"﴾ ﴿of the greatest losers﴾. Since their deeds were diverse, for among them are those who worship the angels, among them those who worship the stars, among them those who worship some of the prophets, among them those who worship idols, and among them those who disbelieve in other than these, He gathered the distinguishing term and said: ﴿in deeds﴾.

Then He described them with the opposite of what they claim for themselves of success in endeavor and excellence in works, so He said: ﴿Those whose effort has gone astray﴾, that is, deviated from the right course and so became void, ﴿in the life of this world﴾, by turning away from Him who alone benefits and harms them, and by turning toward that which has neither benefit nor harm in it. ﴿While they﴾, that is, while the state is that they, despite this being clear like the sun, ﴿think﴾, because of the weakness of their intellects, ﴿that they are doing good work﴾, that is, an act that is at the utmost of soundness, while they are at the utmost of ignorance of it.

Al-Bukhari related in (p-148) the Book of Tafsir, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the greatest losers are the Jews and the Christians. He said: As for the Jews, they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food [in it] nor drink. The end of the quotation. I say: Likewise the Jews said so, because both groups denied the bodily resurrection and restricted it to the spiritual.

Since they denied that they were at fault in this, because they clung to many good deeds far removed from error, he explained to them the cause of the futility of their striving, saying: ﴿Those﴾ [i.e.] the far-removed, the hateful ones, ﴿are those who disbelieved﴾, meaning they cast a veil and covering over what ought to be made manifest and made known, while belittling ﴿the signs of their Lord﴾ from His speech and His acts. He explained the cause of this disbelief by saying: ﴿and in the meeting with Him﴾, meaning they no longer feared, so nothing turned them back from their desires. ﴿So their deeds became void﴾, meaning they fell, were nullified and corrupted by reason of their denial of the proofs. ﴿Their deeds﴾, because they were not built on the foundation of faith. ﴿So We shall not﴾, meaning that as a consequence of their falling, ﴿We shall not assign to them﴾, by the greatness and majesty that We possess, which bar anyone from objecting to Us or interceding with Us without Our permission, ﴿any weight on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning We will not regard them, because they ignored Our command, which is nothing more evident than it, and felt secure from Our plan, which is nothing more dangerous than it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 18, verse 106:

(p-149) Since this context indicates that they have Hell clearer than the sun, He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the great matter that We have made clear of their threat, ﴿is their recompense﴾. However, since it was governed by their misguidance and obtuseness, He clarified the recompense with His saying: ﴿Hell﴾, and He made the causation explicit with His saying: ﴿because they disbelieved﴾, i.e., they committed the covering up of the proofs, ﴿and took My signs﴾, which, despite their illumination, are the most serious of matters and the furthest thing from jest, ﴿and My messengers﴾, who were supported by My manifest acts, along with what they possess of nobility and excellence, ﴿as a mockery﴾. They were not content with disbelief, which is an attack on divinity, until they added to it mockery, which is the greatest contempt.

When He had explained what awaits one of the two groups of those gathered (on the Day of Gathering), as a warning against them, He explained what awaits the other, as a reply to a question that the situation calls for, as an encouragement to follow them and to take them as models. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾, meaning those who actually entered into faith, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, as confirmation of their faith, ﴿from among the good qualities﴾, ﴿will have as their lodging the Gardens of Firdaws﴾, meaning the gardens of paradise's highest level. Its origin is the orchard (bustan), which is truly a garden, because whatever lies below it is lower than it, and because of the abundance of its trees, which conceal whoever enters it. ﴿As a lodging (nuzul)﴾, just as the blazing fire and the shackles were a lodging for those people, prepared for them upon entry.

Abiding therein, after their entry; they do not desire (lā yabghūna) any removal (ḥiwalan) from it, meaning they do not wish for the slightest desire, [that is, "no change" (taḥawwulan)], because there is nothing beyond it, to repel what might be imagined, namely that the matter is as it is in this world, where everyone in whatever bliss he is in would desire what is higher than it, because long residence may bring weariness. Rather, they are in the utmost contentment with it, because of the kinds of delights in it that have no limit or end; none of them desires anything other than what he has, whether he is in al-Firdaws or in what is below it. This is an allusion to the disbelievers, who cry out in the Fire: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out from it﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 107]. This is the reverse of what was in this world, of the disbelievers' inclination toward it and their love for long remaining in it, and the believers' detachment from it and their longing for their Lord through leaving it.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 18, verse 109:

When the answer to their questions had been completed in the best manner, interwoven with the clear proofs you see and the precious points that bind them to a decisive resolution of the dispute, and He followed that with the account of the matter whose neglect had emboldened them to disbelieve, which is the matter of the Resurrection, and ended it with what implies that His known things cannot be limited, because His power over the bliss of the people of Paradise has no end and so cannot be counted, and the Jews had objected to His words at its beginning, ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾ [al-Isra': 85], on the grounds that they had been given the Torah, and because for each of the questions they asked, with their long tails of matters, there were matters that are astonishing, [and perhaps -] someone said: Why does He not increase that in explanation? He, exalted is He, said, commanding (p-151) the answer to all of that, informing them that they cannot reach the completion of the explanation of any one of His known things, nor the final exhaustion of any one of His powers, cutting them off from questioning and bringing it close to their understanding through a kind of example: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O noblest of creation, to them: ﴿If the sea were﴾, that is, its water, despite its greatness in your sight, ﴿ink﴾, and it is a name for what the inkwell is supplied with of ink, ﴿for the words﴾, that is, for writing the words of ﴿my Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to me in describing that and other things, of what you have over-pressed in asking about what you asked about or other than that, ﴿would surely be exhausted﴾, that is, it would perish with a perishing that has no remedy, ﴿the sea﴾, because it is a finite body.

Since created things, by virtue of being contingent (mumkinah), possess in themselves nothing but non-existence, and since the words are among the attributes of God, and the attributes of God are of necessary existence (wajib al-wujud), their exhaustion is impossible. Thus the exhaustion of the contingent, of the sea and what supplies it, in comparison with them, would encompass all times. He stripped the time-adverb of the preposition (harf al-jarr) and said: ﴿before﴾, that is, it would be spent and emptied, ﴿the words of my Lord﴾ are exhausted, because they have no limit, since His known things and His powers have no limit, and each of them has a long explanation and a grave, weighty matter. And since no one other than Him is able to supply the sea, He said: ﴿And even if We brought﴾, that is, with what We have of greatness that does not belong to anyone other than Us, ﴿the like of it as a supply﴾, that is, to it, which would be written with it, it would also be exhausted. All of this is a metonymy (kinayah) for the absence of exhaustion, because it is a conditional on what is customarily impossible, like their saying: "You will not cease to be upon such-and-such as long as a sea moistens a tuft of wool and the night darkens," and the like. Perhaps He expressed it with the sound plural (jam' al-salamah), to indicate that if the little of them is in this abundance, then how about what is more than that? That is a matter that does not fall under any description. He expressed it with "before" rather than saying "and they were not exhausted" and the like, because that suffices to cut them off from pursuing the questioning to its limit, and because expressing it in such a manner might open a door of over-pressing, which is that they would make the waw a waw of circumstance (waw al-hal), making the exhaustion conditioned by that. As for Surah Luqman, the context of its composition established its contents upon ﴿the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Luqman: 26], and its purpose is that the expression in it should be other than what is here; so each surah's expression is most eloquent in relation to its context. Yet neither of the two expressions, in its explicit form, indicates the exhaustion of the words or its absence, while in the understanding of each of them, through reflecting on the indicators within the context and elsewhere, there is that which decisively establishes their non-exhaustion. There is no contradiction between the two verses, even if the expression in this surah is more inclined toward ambiguity (tashabbuh). It is answered with what they said about a line of the poet, "upon a faint trail whose landmark does not guide one," that what falls within the scope of negation does not necessarily imply existence. Perhaps the expression with such things is among the trials that distinguish between him in whose heart is sickness and the firmly rooted one who refers the ambiguous to the clear, which is what the decisive proof indicates: that God, exalted is He, has no end to His essence, nor to any (p-153) of His attributes, but He is the First and the Last, the Enduring without cessation. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah (chapter) 18, verse 110:

Since they might say, "What is wrong with you that you do not tell us about these matters, all that we ask you about, whenever we ask you?" And they had denied that the Prophet could be a human being, and had permitted that God could be a stone, and they had made their faith in him conditional upon matters they asked him to perform, as was mentioned after their first questions, namely the Spirit, and the last of them was "Glory be to Him" [i.e. the request for God to bring angels as witnesses]. And it had been established, from their answers to the questions in this manner, that he was a messenger, so He, glorified be He, commanded him to answer them concerning all of that with what would refute their error and expose their doubts, guiding them to the most important matter for them, the letter (of the Qur'an) on which the whole dispute revolves, which is monotheism (tawhid). So He said: ﴿Say: "I am only a human being like you"﴾, i.e., in seeking help through the power to bring the non-existent into existence and in reporting the unseen; ﴿a human being like you﴾, i.e., I have no command and no power except what my Lord empowers me with, and there is no reason to find my messengership from God strange, for that is His practice with those before me. ﴿It is revealed to me﴾ [i.e. -] from God, who has singled me out for the message, just as He revealed to the messengers before me what no one can do without knowing and believing. ﴿That your God is﴾ (p-154) and He pointed out that His divinity is absolute, not dependent on the making of any maker or anything else, so He said: ﴿One God﴾, i.e., He is not divided by any homogeneity or otherwise, able to do what He wills, with no rival to Him, and He did not delay the answer to what you asked me about out of inability, ignorance, or [any] contempt [for me] by Him. This is what it is important for everyone to know. As for what you asked about concerning the matter of the Spirit and the two stories, as a means of testing, it is a matter that, if you were ignorant of it, its ignorance would not harm you; but if you follow me, you would know it now, and what it indicates of the matter of the Hour, by faith in the unseen, as knowledge of certainty (ilm al-yaqin), and you would know it after death by witnessing, as the eye of certainty (ayn al-yaqin), and by direct experience, as the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). If you do not follow me, its knowledge will not benefit you. ﴿So whoever﴾, i.e., there results from His oneness, which entails His power, that whoever ﴿hopes﴾, i.e., believes in His recompensing him for his deeds in the Hereafter, by seeing Him and otherwise. He said ﴿the meeting with his Lord﴾ only as an alert that He is the one who does good to everyone by His sole creating and providing, with no partner in any of that, according to the analogy of what we know: that there is no owner who does not dominate his property at his meeting, directing it in his commands morning and evening.

Since the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, it is obligatory for the servant to be sincere in his action, just as his Lord's action was in nurturing him by bringing him into existence and what follows. So He said: ﴿let him do﴾, and emphasized it to inform that, together with affirmation (tasdiq), there must be acknowledgment (iqrar), so He said: ﴿deeds﴾, i.e., even if it is little, ﴿righteous﴾, which is what He commands him, (p-155) of the principles of religion and its branches, from monotheism and other things, of deeds of the heart, body, and wealth, in order to be safe from His punishment; ﴿and let him not associate﴾, i.e., that deed should be founded upon the basis, which is that he does not associate, even by showing off, ﴿in the worship of his Lord anyone﴾. So when he does [that], he succeeds and attains the knowledge of this world and the Hereafter. The end of the surah has corresponded to its beginning by describing the words of God and then what is revealed to him, and each of them is more general than the Book in its being most upright, calling to the safest state, on the most upright path, which is monotheism, away from a partner, more general than a son and other things, and excellence in action, together with good tidings for those who believe and warning for those who turn away from the signs and the reminder. Thus it has become clear that God, the Exalted, by His oneness, His perfect knowledge, and the comprehensiveness of His power, has the attributes of perfection, so it is correct that He alone deserves all praise. And God is the Granter of success, and praise be to God for completing the surah of al-Kahf from the book *Nazm al-Durar min Tanasub al-Ayi was-Suwar*.
